Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo last week — DataCove's security team asked us to get a concise write-up on a few items before we proceed to procurement. Can you confirm the following at a high level?

1) Which cloud regions does Redwood run inference in for hosted customers? Are there region pins available (we're US-first but have some EU data).
2) Who are the current subprocessors that may touch customer inputs (inference requests, logs, metrics)? A short list is fine; we may ask for evidence later.
3) Do you ever move data cross-border for batching, cache, or backup? If so, under what controls?

Hi Morgan —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; attaching our subprocessor map and region summary for reference. I looped in Aditya (legal) and Neha (platform) for any nitty-gritty details you might request.

1) Regions / compute locality:
- Hosted (default): we operate in multiple public cloud regions across US, EU, and APAC. For most customers, inference is routed to the nearest region by default for latency.
- Region pinning: we support region pinning for hosted accounts on a per-project basis (US-only or EU-only). This is a subscription setting and can be enforced at the tenant level.

2) Subprocessors that may handle request data (summary):
- Cloud compute providers (AWS, GCP) — GPUs and ephemeral compute.
- Object storage for optional artifacts (S3/GCS) — used for model artifacts and optional user-uploaded files.
- Monitoring & metrics (Datadog) — metrics and anonymized latency/error telemetry.
- Logging & tracing (Cloud logging services) — request identifiers and redacted traces; payloads are not stored by default.
- Optional third-party integrations (transcription, OCR) — used only when customer enables the feature.

3) Cross-border movements and controls:
- We do not routinely copy raw customer input for inference to secondary regions.
- Short-lived KV/prefix caches may be routed to the same region as compute; we do not batch-request across regions unless a customer permits multi-region routing.
- Backups of persistent artifacts (model files, customer-config) are stored per the tenant's region by default; cross-region replication is opt-in and disabled for region-pinned tenants.

See attached PDF for the subprocessor roster and a region matrix. If you need SOC/SLA artifacts, Aditya can drive that next.

Best,

Morgan —

Quick clarifications from legal/compliance side:

- Subprocessor list (attached) is current as of May 2027. We include contact emails for each vendor and the category of processing (compute, storage, monitoring).
- Data residency guarantee: for region-pinned tenants we contractually commit to keep customer inference traffic and derived metadata within the pinned region. This is in the DPA; we can provide a redline for procurement.
- Cross-border transfers: we use standard contractual mechanisms where required (SCCs) for transfers outside of the EU when customers are not region-pinned. For regulated customers wanting additional controls, we offer our Private deployment option (VPC/on-prem).

If you need a signed SCC pack or SOC 2 report, please let me know and we'll start the evidence delivery.

Hi Morgan —

A) Logs & telemetry: for region-pinned tenants, request logs and telemetry are retained and processed in-region. We do forward anonymized/aggregated telemetry to centralized monitoring for platform health, but that stream excludes raw request payloads. The detail is in the attached region summary.

B) Cache TTL & movement: KV/prefix caches are short-lived by default (configurable; default 10–20 minutes). We do not proactively move cached items between regions for load balancing — caching is per-region unless you opt into multi-region routing.

C) Vendor export: yes — Aditya's attached CSV contains vendor contacts and processing categories. We'll prepare a filtered export that highlights vendors that may see unredacted inputs (for many customers that's only the cloud GPU provider and optional transcription partners). Expect that by EOD; we'll redact emails for vendors that never touch payloads.

Next steps: I'll drop the filtered vendor list and the SOC pack link into HubSpot (HS-DC-7412) and can set up a call with Neha if the infra team wants to review network/topology diagrams.
